decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through contacts extend existing drilling and bonding capabilities at low holding cost, and wafer-level packaging demand is still resolving, so the option stays open.
The small-diameter carrier wafer sits in the firm's core thin-wafer handling business, costs almost nothing to keep and fits the push toward reusable carriers.
The Cu-interposer is a flagship growth option in advanced packaging whose value is still uncertain but rising, so a further commitment is justified rather than abandonment.
The Wafer Universe off-the-shelf brand uses existing standard products and channels at low cost and broadens market reach, with no evidence that its value is failing.

Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the core and more costly to pursue, but glass substrates for packaging are gaining interest, so management keeps this small option open a while longer while watching for clearer demand signals.
